Author: Samit Gopal
Bench: Samit Gopal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:92465
Court No. - 64
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 13514 of 2025
Applicant :- Anjan
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Vipin Kumar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.
1.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: List revised.
2. Heard Sri Vipin Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Ajay Singh, learned AGA-I for the State and perused the material on record.

3. This bail application under Section 483 of B.N.S.S. has been filed by the applicant Anjan, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No. 54 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304-B I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, registered at Police Station Tezi Bazar, District Jaunpur.

4. A report by the District Judge concerned was called for by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 01.05.2025 for clarifying as to whether the applicant is in jail in the present matter for Anjan vs State Of U.P. on 29 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68572263/
1 offence under Section 302 IPC or not.
The office has placed the said report on record through its office report dated 13.05.2025.
Subsequently vide order dated 15.05.2025 learned counsel for the applicant was permitted to make the necessary correction in the prayer clause of the bail application.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that he has done so.
The perusal of the records show that from the prayer of the bail application Section 302 IPC has been deleted.

Charge Sheet No. A-57 dated 12.04.2024 in the present matter has been submitted against the applicant under Sections 498-A, 304-B IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act.
5.

The FIR of the matter was lodged on 29.03.2024 under Sections 498-A, 304-B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act by Gulhasan against the applicant alleging therein that his sister Shama was married to Anjan the applicant about five years back.
The applicant used to demand money from her regularly.
On 29.03.2024 he received an information that Shama has committed suicide by hanging.
On the said information he and other persons of the village went to the said place and found his sister lying on the bed.
On enquiry it transpired that she died at 07:30 am.
Report be lodged and action be taken.

6. The postmortem examination of Smt. Shama was conducted on 29.03.2024 in which the doctor found a single ligature mark on her body and the cause of death was opined as asphyxia as a result of antemortem hanging.

7. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that vide order dated 19.04.2024 the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jaunpur has taken cognizance on the charge sheet against the applicant for offences under Sections 498-A, 304-B IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act.

It is further submitted that charges in the matter have been framed by the Sessions Judge, Jaunpur vide order dated 11.07.2024 under Sections 498-A, 304-B, 302 IPC and Section 4 D.P. Act, certified photocopy of summoning order dated 19.04.2024 and the order framing charge dated 11.07.2024 have been placed before the Court for the same which are annexure 6 and 7 respectively to the affidavit.
8.
Learned counsel for the State submits that the remand of the applicant in the present matter is only under Sections 498-A, 304-B IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act.
The Sessions Judge, Jaunpur vide report dated 08.05.2025 has reported that the applicant is lodged in jail under Sections 498-A, 304-B IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act.
It is further reported that Section 302 IPC is not mentioned in his custody warrant.
9. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that although the applicant is the husband of the deceased but he has been falsely implicated in the present case.

It is submitted that the deceased committed suicide and died which is suggestive from the postmortem examination report wherein the doctor found a single ligature mark and the cause of death is asphyxia as a result of antemortem hanging.

While placing para 20 of the affidavit it is submitted that the marriage of the applicant with the deceased was solemnized on 25.08.2018 and they were leading a happy married life but since the deceased was issueless she was under depression and on its account she committed suicide.
It is submitted that there is no reference whatsoever that there was any demand of dowry but there is only an allegation that the applicant regularly used to demand money.

It is submitted that subsequently during investigation the first informant for the first time stated that there was a Anjan vs State Of U.P. on 29 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68572263/
2 demand of dowry by the applicant.
It is submitted that the same is an afterthought and just in order to implicate the applicant.

It is submitted that the applicant has no criminal history as stated in para 30 of the affidavit and is in jail since 31.03.2024.
10.

Per contra, learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that there is an allegation of demand of money by the applicant in the FIR and subsequently during investigation it is stated that dowry was also demanded, the deceased died within seven years of marriage in her matrimonial house and the death is unnatural.
The applicant is named in the FIR and he is the husband of the deceased.
11. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that there is no other bodily injury received except for the ligature mark on the body of the deceased.
The cause of death is asphyxia as a result of antemortem hanging.

The FIR states that there was a demand of money by the applicant and subsequently during investigation the first informant is stated that there is a demand of dowry.
12.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of evidence and also the absence of any convincing material to indicate the possibility of tampering with the evidence, this Court is of the view that the applicant may be enlarged on bail.

13. Let the applicant Anjan, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
ii) The applicant will abide the orders of court, will attend the court on every date and will not delay the disposal of trial in any manner whatsoever.
(iii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iv) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.

(v) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement Anjan vs State Of U.P. on 29 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68572263/
3 under Section 313 Cr.P.C. If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law and the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A IPC.

(vi) The trial court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously after the release of the applicant.
14.

The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
15. The bail application is allowed.
16. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

Order Date :- 29.5.2025 M. ARIF (Samit Gopal, J.)
